You heard 10x demand for compute > supply from $CRWV today. 

Hearing from $TSM today on Nikkei Forum: 

"The demand on our leading node [most advanced] silicon is insatiable"

Customers "want to get [their] hands around any compute capability they can have. It's truly an insatiable environment."

Q: Whether AI demand was slowing?
A: "we did not see any sign of slowdown"

Q: How demand compared with TSMC’s ability to supply
A: "the demand actually is still far above our capability today to supply."

TSMC identified power and substrates as bottlenecks customers were encountering. 

On the mid-to-high-50s annualized growth estimate for AI accelerator revenue from 2024 to 2029. Wei said "it probably will be higher."

Describing things as "insatiable" from a traditionally conservative company... doesn't quite look like any collapse in AI demand.

quoted_tweet.text:
$CRWV ER and read through for $NBIS and other Neoclouds:

“We have 10x as much qualified demand as available capacity”.

- interest in 2028 capacity already amounts to several times what CoreWeave has available

-  CoreWeave raised prices by 25% in July, +10% later in Q3, and more to come in Q4

- Ampere and Hopper rental pricing rose 30–50% quarter over quarter (older GPUs)

- better financing conditions (higher prepayments, lower interest 7–7.5% for new loans)

-  positive adjusted net income in the first half of 2028.

So we’re seeing higher pricing esp. for older GPUs…better financing mechanics, and extreme demand imbalance where you have 10x demand > supply.

Same issues are there for this company in specific with interest rates, but I’d argue other Neoclouds are in a better spot.

But it’s wild to witness AI infrastructure names crash while demand keeps growing

There's a lot of news about WT (3036) introducing their first CW DFB laser line card. 

More significant than people think for medium-long term. For economic impact and what revenue looks like: 

- $SMTC generated 74% of its revenue through distributors. $AMBA as another example, ~60-70% of their 2026 revenue went through this company.

- With WT in specific, if you look at even a large company like $AVGO scaled: 

-> 13% of Broadcom revenue went through WT in 2020 
->  18% (2021) 
-> 20% (2022) 
-> ~21% (2023) 
-> ~28% (2024) 
-> now possibly up to ~46% (they stopped naming)

Just showing how important the largest distributors in the world become to semi companies. 

Given how WT chairman attributed rapid growth coming from AI photonics demand (eg. DSPs to optical module makers):

It becomes more interesting for a certain company that WT introduced their first CW DFB laser line card during an industry bottleneck.

This aged pretty well, when I said this last year in 2025, Clickhouse was a $6.7B company... 

Now as an update, their secondary valuation sits around ~$50B, which $NBIS owns 25%+ of. 

I've always liked Nebius the most because sum of parts, with all their lesser known subsidiaries growing alongside their core neocloud business.

Including Avride (self-driving), Clickhouse, Toloka, and other subsidiaries that they owned.  

This year Nebius also acquired:
- Tavily (web search and retrival)
- Clarifai (Inference orchestration)

Which scale independently as well (the others were integrated into Nebius Token Factory).

Hard to view $NBIS as just another neocloud when it has billions in scaling value outside its core infrastructure business.

You can build a working budget or client tracker in Claude this week. No Excel, no formulas. 24,000 people saved the announcement overnight, and Microsoft dropped 3% in 30 minutes.

Claude Sheets shipped on Monday (beta, paid plans). You ask for a tracker or a budget and you get a working spreadsheet you can keep building.

Here's the trap. You type "make me a tracker" and you get five columns and no logic. The sheet is exactly as good as the brief you gave it.

Two prompts, in this order:

Prompt 1: The brief (Opus 5.5, in Claude Sheets)
"Before building anything, ask me 6 questions, one at a time: what I'm tracking, where the numbers come from (manual, export, an app), how often I update it, who else reads it, the 3 decisions I make from it, and what breaks in my current setup. Then propose the structure: tabs, columns, which cells are inputs and which are formulas, and 3 checks that catch my mistakes (totals that must match, dates out of range, duplicates). Wait for my OK, then build it. No sample data that looks real. Put every assumption in a Notes tab."

Prompt 2: The audit (Fable 5.2, once. It shipped a day earlier, caught a bank statement where deposits didn't match the balance in Anthropic's tests, and counts for up to 50% of your weekly Pro limit, so one pass is enough)
"Here is my spreadsheet. Don't rebuild it. Check every formula against what its column header promises. Find circular logic, hard-coded numbers that should be inputs, and totals that silently skip rows. Give me a table: cell, problem, fix, severity. Then list the 3 assumptions most likely to be wrong for a business like mine. Max 300 words."

Excel didn't lose to a chat box. It lost to people who never liked formulas and now don't have to write them.

You can grab more business prompts in the God of Prompt library. 7,200+ prompts, free, no signup. Link in the first reply.

Would you move your business tracker out of Excel this month, or wait until Sheets is out of beta?
